headline: Citizen Lab exposes zero-click spyware delivered via targeted online ads
summary: Citizen Lab researchers at the University of Toronto disclosed the first technical evidence of mercenary spyware delivered through targeted online advertising, compromising devices at Al Jazeera Media Network without any user interaction. An Israeli adtech company was implicated in enabling the delivery. Outlets differed on what to call the spyware or software involved, variously naming it AdFection, Candiru spyware, and Discover-Tech's Controlium.

claims.statement: Citizen Lab released the first technical evidence of mercenary spyware being distributed via online advertising.

sources.quote: Researchers at The Citizen Lab have for the first time released technical evidence of sophisticated mercenary spyware being distributed via online advertising.
The incident is likely 1st confirmation of mercenary spyware delivered by targeted ads.

claims.statement: Devices at Al Jazeera Media Network were compromised in a zero-click attack via malicious online ads, requiring no user interaction.

sources.quote: dozens of devices at media organization Al Jazeera were hacked after being shown malicious online ads.
Candiru spyware was delivered to devices at Al Jazeera Media Network via targeted online advertisements in a zero-click attack that required only rendering the malicious ads on the victim's device.

claims.statement: An Israeli advertising/adtech company was implicated in enabling the spyware's delivery.

sources.quote: An Israeli advertising agency has been serving millions of online adverts that allow “zero-click” spyware to be used against targets
Israeli adtech outfit allegedly helped spyware vendors infect phones while enjoying Google's seal of approval

claims.statement: One outlet identified the spyware as a new type dubbed 'AdFection.'

sources.quote: A new type of spyware dubbed "AdFection" is infecting phones and computers via global online advertising networks.

claims.statement: Another outlet identified the spyware as Candiru spyware.

sources.quote: Zero-click attacks used targeted ads to deliver Candiru spyware

claims.statement: Another outlet named the implicated software Discover-Tech's Controlium.

sources.quote: Discover-Tech’s Controlium software lets clients mass-profile internet users then covertly hack targets

discrepancies.explanation: Outlets gave different names for the spyware or software involved in the same ad-delivered campaign -- 'AdFection,' Candiru spyware, and Discover-Tech's Controlium.

quotes.quote: A new type of spyware dubbed "AdFection" is infecting phones and computers via global online advertising networks.
Zero-click attacks used targeted ads to deliver Candiru spyware
